notes.title: SMYS 1.0 is OUT NOW!
notes.content:
[b]Happy launch day! [/b]

After a year and 7 major updates the game is no longer in Early Access and now features all of its content.

There are still small things to fix here and there, and surely bugs that have not been reported to me yet (especially with the constant flow of added content that could have generate new ones), which is why I'm leaving the bug report panel in the game so players can continue sending in any issue they encounter while playing.

No more content is currently planned for the game even tho a 5th picking phase have been designed and could be added at some point if we can afford to. More updates will follow to fix the current and upcoming bugs and to improve what already is in the game.

Have fun!

notes.title: Environmental Disturbance - Major Update
notes.content:
We finally reached the end of the Early Access roadmap! It was a quite a journey but we made it. 
[b]The game will officially exit Early Access on May 15th. [/b]


[h2]Building Phase Events[/h2]

Taking into account all the feedback we received since the Early Access release, what comes out of it is most players prefer playing Picking Phases than Building Phases. So to address it we decided to add special events that will randomly occur during most Building Phases.

[b]Meadawn[/b]
As the first Building Phase to have been featured in the game, we decided to keep this one as it is. That way if some players still want to without any events they can do so by disabling every other Building Phases in the game configurator.

[b]Jungle Night [/b]
In the jungles of the world of SMYS lives an uncommon type of primate, the moonkey. They live by night and will come steal your stuff if you're not careful.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/9971bd466a8d8d26b46f54d83ea967de9afd7dc3.gif[/img]

[b]Frozen Canyon [/b]
It's been called a canyon since the start but the ground was flat, now there are 3 different ground layouts with holes in them. It will force you to place your blocks differently to build bridges above the holes to then reach the yumyum, also you can fall in the holes obviously.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/fcb28a5353e0effb9674527bb6f88912924557f0.gif[/img]

[b]Lava Chambers [/b]
The lava chambers are within an active volcano that will occasionally wake up and the lava will rise up. Don't stay on the floor or you'll get burnt!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/e5e0e315a8da0e379a8965ce020040a394bd4b17.gif[/img]

[h2]New Soundtracks[/h2]
The Vanta Black game mode and Time Attack game mode finally have their own dedicated soundtrack. All soundtracks are now done and will soon be available as a DLC for anyone wanting to further support us.

[h2]New Achievement Icons[/h2]
Every single one of the 52 achievements now have a dedicated icon, here is a look at all of them :

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/950ee719657a73848c79c66623057abc6393ed5d.jpg[/img]

notes.title: SMYS Classic, the original game idea
notes.content:
[h2]An Endless Feature Creeping Story[/h2]

Back in 2019 when we first designed the game, it was quite different from what it is today.

The game had no bonuses, no minigames, no collection system, no games modes, and it was entirely focused on the stairs building aspect. It was quite a simple game but happened to grow into something way bigger than what we planned for.

This is why I eventually decided to publish a 'Classic' version of the game, the game almost as we first designed it.

[b]The Classic version will be released as a free game on Steam in April 2024[/b].

Here is a look at one of the first concept art we made for the game :
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/9f9a12006ebb19ae18be96cee22577799eab394a.png[/img]

And here is a screenshot from the Classic version :
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/6a7426089cacfd48c68493c820b930063bf2ff86.png[/img]

It looks similar to the main game mode from the final version of the project, but plays different. There is a lot more strategy that comes into play as both collecting items and building stairs happen at the same time, which adds a resource management aspect to the game.

Also compared to the first design, and as we added bonuses to the final version, I decided to keep some of them in the classic version, including : Bomb, Upside Down, Smoke Bomb, Items Generation, and Structural Reinforcement. Not having them in the game seemed like missing on so much fun and we might have had them added to the game anyway so here you have it.

If you already own the final version of the game I still encourage you to wishlist the game (or play if it's already out) as said priviously it plays different and you could consider it as an additional game mode.


https://store.steampowered.com/app/2879490/

notes.content:
With this newest major update, the game now has most of its content available and what's left will be added at the same time as the game fully releases into version 1.0 later this month.

[h2]Bumpy Cranes[/h2]

In this new picking phase, you play in a 1v1 configuration against a member of the opposing team. 

Each player has its own crane that he can move to grab items to be used later in the building phase, but as you're playing on the same rail as another player you will have to fight for space control by pushing the other player back to his side bumper cars style.

notes.title: Thermal Shock - Major Update
notes.content:
This major update includes not one but [b]two[/b] new building phases alongside a lot of improvements for the game. Everything that is included in this update was supposed to be published as 3 separate updates but we decided to change our plans and publish 1 huge update instead.

[h2]Lava Chambers[/h2]

This new building phase has a unique feature, it's played in the gloomy and dark caves of the lava biome. All the colors are inverted and the only lighting is coming from the background which leads to some shadow like play.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/a9706938a1ddf95e173eb4f090a42ef8070908f3.png[/img]

[h2]Frozen Canyon[/h2]

At the complete opposite of Lava Chambers, this building phase takes place in the middle of blizzardy canyons in which you'll eventually have to watch your steps to not fall into the abyss.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/8c1d1465dad8c696de2bc608afc28668f764abe0.png[/img]

[h2]Roadmap Changes & Early Access End[/h2]

I've shared infos about it on Twitter earlier this year, but Online Multiplayer has been removed from the roadmap for now. To keep things short, I am using Unity as the engine to make the game and it's been quite a wild ride lately, which unfortunately impacted the studio. At the end of the day I can't be developing the game without funding, and as most of it is currently coming from Unity related sources the situation is looking pretty dire.

It is also, funny enough, one of the reasons this update is so content rich, all I can do is work extra hard and hope things get better with the release of the game in the upcoming weeks. Maybe if some kind of miracle happens I'll be able to get funding to continue developing the game past release but I would rather not count on it so we'll see how it goes.

There are 2 nodes left on the roadmap, the last picking phase 'Bumpy Cranes', and the last major update which will actually happen at the same time as the game releases and will include the addition of special events to building phases.

Bug fixing has been great thanks to the players' feedback and reports. It's quite stable right now and reports of new bugs are rare, which allows us to focus on polishing the game for the release.


[b]Thanks to all of you who've played or shared the game around, it trully helps.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/39c61a6a266ce0ba8da561abbb321eed238a152b.gif[/img]

[h2]Achievements[/h2]

The addition of a collection system such as the yums book is the perfect time to add achievements support to the game, there are 52 of them to obtain right now and I'm planning to add more in the future with the upcoming updates. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/cd27d58f54e01adf369193d3479793ecf674c8f1.png[/img]

All of them currently have the same icon, unique icons for each achievement are in the work.

[h2]Steam Cloud[/h2]

It was supposed to be part of this update but actually went live earlier this month, the game now supports Steam Cloud for saving all your game data so you can keep your progress across all your devices.

To encourage players to send more feedback and share about the issues they encounter, the bug report button has been moved back to the main menu. A new feedback button has been also added to separate issues and general feedback/suggestions.

notes.title: Arsenal - Major Update
notes.content:
[h2]New Bonuses[/h2]

The game now includes 6 new bonuses, which raises the total to 10.

It was initially planned to have 4 added but I felt like some more ideas were worth the extra development time.

So here are the 6 new bonuses and what they do :

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/7b602752d40732ff87f04ac5470edf5c3d19fbd7.png[/img]

[h2]Game Configurator[/h2]

Each time new content is added into the game, there is a risk players don't like a specific new thing and would rather keep playing the game without it. 

It is now possible with the new in-game configurator : disable anything from picking phases, building phases, blocks, bonuses, and play the game YOUR way. 

It also allows for fun new ways to play the game, like playing with only 1 type of block, or only destructive bonuses, and this will keep expanding even after Early Access as we keep adding new content.

You can find the game configurator in the Settings panel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/cfed4573575320e68d592a42447b282e893a2347.png[/img]

[h2]Next Major Update[/h2]

The next major update that should be available before the end of 2023 is Yums Book.

It will include a collection system, cloud saving, and achievements.

notes.title: Vanta Black - Major Update
notes.content:
[b]THE FIRST MAJOR UPDATE FOR SMYS IS HERE[/b]

From quality of life improvements to accessibility, this first major update is taking the game to a whole new level. 

The game being the most fun when playing as a 4 players party, it is unfortunately not always that easy to have 3 friends available at the same time to play the game, and this is what this update is primarily meant to address.

[h2]Vanta Black[/h2]
Introducing a new game mode : Vanta Black.

Despite being a competitive multiplayer focused game, SMYS has a pretty dense lore on which we rely on when adding new content to the game. When thinking about ways to make the game more accessible, Vanta immediately came to our mind as a character that would make a great opponent to play against, and this new game mode was born.

Vanta is one of the only zglub that is not drawn towards eating yumyums, as he was originally cursed after eating the moonyum, out of despair, erasing all sense of taste he ever had. He is now driven by his sole jealousy and wants to prevent his siblings from being able to enjoy these delicacies yumyums are.

You will face him, either solo or with a friend, in a relentless battle to the top. As the world's tallest and strongest zglub, Vanta will not be easy to beat, especially if you're going one on one with him. This is a real challenge aimed at players looking for a strong opponent, and while it may start easy, the difficulty quickly ramps up with Vanta using new powerful abilities each round.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/ca7dd4b3663924529814dd81c5c59a6db0c6ed0e.jpg[/img]

Playing this mode with a friend is obviously easier, and I hope that players with a less competitive mindset can enjoy it this way.


[h2]Bots for Multiplayer[/h2]
This has been requested by the players, weither it is to be able to play alone, or to fill an uneven party of 3 with an additional player. 

I did not realize how important this was until it was part of the game, and I'm glad I listened to the players feedback as it is undeniably adding a lot of value to the game, making it accessible and fun to small parties. Even playing as a party of 2 with each one a bot is suprisingly loads of fun, I'd even go with saying it was more fun than playing 1v1 without bots.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/f6e6316541712d19f47f0b6ffeeec169b6048b43.jpg[/img]

The only limitation I did put on this is that you can only spawn up to 2 AIs for now, which should address most requests I had about adding bots, but if players request it I'll make it 3 so a player could play alone as a party of 4, 1 AI teaming up with the player against 2 AIs.

The bots difficulty can be modified in the settings menu to suit players needs by adjusting either their playing speed or if they should use bonuses or not. I'll add more settings in future updates as I improve AI's behaviors.

Bots have been playtested for hundreds of hours by now, and while I fixed close to 100% of the errors I've found, there might be specific cases we did not encounter yet, which I hope the players will report to me so they can be fixed.

I am publishing a progress roadmap every sunday on Twitter and Mastodon on which you can see how far each upcoming update is from making it into the game, feel free to follow me there to stay updated about your most anticipated updates.

notes.title: Last Fixes Before EA & Store Re-skin
notes.content:
We already started working on Online Multiplayer and upcoming updates, you can check out the roadmap that we published on the store page to know what we're preparing.

Note that the roadmap will probably change as we receive feedback from players. Each update may feature major changes that are not specifically implied in the title, for instance the "Yums' Book" update will also include Steam Achievements for the game.

Online Multiplayer represents a huge load of work and while it's our number one priority it may not be the first update to be available. We want content to be available for the players as soon as it's ready.

The game is releasing in Early Access tomorrow and we hope you'll join us to make this game as good as it can be.

notes.title: Localization Update - French, Spanish, Italian, German
notes.content:
[h2]First Localization Update[/h2] 

This update features French, Spanish, Italian, and German translation.
You can find a new Language section in Settings where you can set your prefered language from the now 5 different languages available.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/0604d0e7fd1a1daa9f83f745c641cf93765d08a7.png[/img]

We only speak English, French, and Spanish, so we hope every other languages translation is decent. 
If you find anything odd in the translation of languages we don't speak, feel free to use the Report Panel in Settings to share it with us or reach out directly @StarvingFoxStd on Twitter so we can improve it.

More languages are to come in later updates, we already have a few in mind like Chinese, Korean, and Japanese, but feel free to suggest other languages, we'll do our best to add the most requested ones.

notes.title: Bye Mighty Tools, Welcome Yumyums!
notes.content:
[h2]Yumyums[/h2]

You may have noticed on the Steam page that our characters are playing with sweets look alike items and not tools, we've been preparing this transition for a while for the game and it is finally happening, let me introduce you : the Yumyums!

Sixteen are already in the game right now, split among 4 themes (Asia, Planets, Season, Holidays), and more are to come alongside a collection system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/c311229cc67d3d494d25c5119e7172ecd2e4b84a.png[/img]

Note that for this update, only the items sprites have changed and we still have to work on adding new animations and content related to yumyums.


[h2]UI Changes[/h2]

During the Steam Next Fest, we received a lot of feedback, most of which we have already taken into account, like tutorials and game length for example. This update brings more requested features such as a way to see what your next block is going to be, but we had to find a way to add it to the existing UI, and as we failed to do so we decided to completely rework the player panel of the building phase.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/ab4901817b4a89e14710a1fea556c026a1b4bbd9.png[/img]

The panel size now adapts according to how many bonuses you have left in stock and shows you the shape of the next block you're going to get. One of the only thing we kept from the previous panel is the counter telling you how many blocks are left in your library.


[h2]Preparing Localization[/h2]

We thought it would be a good time to start localizing the game, but as soon as we started working on the french translation, we encountered a problem : our font didn't have accents.

This is most certainly something we did not think about, our main concern being finding a font that would fit the game aesthetically, and as bad as it is to have to let down the font we chose, we picked the most resembling one we could find that also had accents.

We already have a few ideas for languages to translate the game into, like French, Spanish, German, ..., but feel free to suggest what language you'd like SMYS to be translated to. We don't have a lot of text in the game, and adding more languages would not be a huge financial cost if we don't translate the Steam page.

[h2]What's Coming Next[/h2]

Well, as you could expect, more content. More picking phases and building phases, as well as more bonuses, but not for the demo. 

We are currently preparing for Early Access and we'd like even the very first EA version to have enough content to justify the price, which will not increase as we progress towards 1.0 release.

A full roadmap will be available on the Steam page as soon as we enter Early Access in the upcoming months.

Most of the updates the demo will receive from now on will be bug fixing and polishing.

notes.title: Game Length Adjustment
notes.content:
When we updated the game with an end goal, we were aiming for each game to be around 20-25 minutes. It turned out we ended up having each game playtime between 40 and 90 minutes, which is way too long compared to the content the demo has.

We decided to change the number of items each team has to collect from 10 to 4, lowering drastically the length of each game.

notes.title: Advanced Tutorials
notes.content:
In this new weekly update, we're adding a complete tutorials panel which can be consulted at all times. Not understanding how to play seemed to be the main concern during the Next Fest, and it had to be addressed first.

With this new panel, comes the removal of the Controls panel, which was showing all commands but was confusing and only helped figuring out controls for the building phase.

Each tutorial has a controls section, a video clip, and a description to ensure it is as easy as possible to understand, weither it is by watching the video, or reading the description, or both.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/930630e0a0b519da7451049bfef66de9c73595f5.png[/img]

The short tutorial screens before each first picking phase will stay, as it prevents having to open the tutorials panel all the time to understand what each minigame is about. We also added controls informations on those.

[h2]Tutorials[/h2]
Since the release of the demo, and basically since people have had their hands on the game, we've had reports about the difficulty to understand straight away how the game (picking phases in particular) is supposed to be played. 

So we decided it was time to add some tutorial screens, similar to what you can find in Mario Party games with a short description and a video clip showing the players what they are supposed to be doing. We'll also add commands to these screens in the next updates.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/b1f8aa53da10c456b7fc8293365c97151dcc1d16.png[/img]

For now they only show the first time you encounter a specific picking phase, they then only reappear if you restart the game, but this may be up to change as we add more picking phases.

[h2]Background animations[/h2]
As we knew a graphic rework was planned, background animations were always put back. But following the recent update featuring the final graphic rework we were waiting for, background animations went back on top of our todolist and here they are.

Some backgrounds still have no animations (Lobby & Trampolines) and these are coming in the next updates.

notes.title: New Picking Phase : Trampolines
notes.content:
[b]The final part of the demo is finally ready and available for all the players to enjoy![/b]

With this new content update, the demo is now almost complete. It will continue to receive polishing and bug fixes updates (especially now that the Steam Fest is knocking at the door), but as we planned 2 picking phases and 1 building phase to be part of the demo we are glad to have reached that point already.

[h2]Trampoline Picking Phase[/h2]

This new picking phase brings a completely different gameplay than the Canons' one that is already available and we think that it will allow the players to envision the potential of the final game that is planned to feature 4 different picking phases and building phases in version 1.0.

[b]How it's played[/b]

Each team starts either on the left or the right side of the screen as always, a geyser appears in the middle and spawns blocks and bonuses. Each geyser generates 4 blocks (2 on each sides) and potentially a bonus on top.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/2b2195c99dbb7de42e655d1ee73bf69d0a369d82.png[/img]

The players can move freely in the scene to catch items they want to add to their personnal library and that they will use in the following building phase.

To collect an item, a player has to throw it in the appropriate collect zone (players spawning on the left side have their collect zone on the left side of the screen while players spawning on the right side have their collect zone on the right side of the screen) without a player of the opposing team catching it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/905f234adfb9ae9eb5c49a4dfb32c37a0b2ca8a7.png[/img]

Once all items have been collected, a new geyser spawns with different items.

All of this is played in a mushroom field, some of which (the reddish ones) are bouncy and will send you up in the air, leading to some pretty interesting moments and epic comebacks.


[h2]Steam Next Fest[/h2]

We are taking part in february's Steam Next Fest and we encourage you to share the game around you and to play during the festival to support us. We will not be streaming the game during the festival, mainly because our internet quality prevents us to do so, but we'll be actively looking at Twitch and Steam during the festival to see if someone is and we'll gladly stop by to see you in action!

We also invite you to tag us on Twitter @StarvingFoxStd or @SMYSGame to share screenshots/videos with us and/or notify us of your stream schedule.

notes.title: Final Visual Rework
notes.content:
[h2]Final Visual Rework[/h2]
Our designer has been experimenting with multiple graphic styles for SMYS since the beginning of its development in 2020. 

I think we can say that she finally decided on one to stick with, and this is what we are bringing you in this update. All sprites have been remade to switch from a painted vector style to this new hand-drawn cartoonish style, but still keeping the spray painted coloring. It brings new challenges for us but we think it's worth the extra effort and we hope it will please the players' eyes.

notes.title: End Game and Team Names
notes.content:
[h2]End game goal[/h2]

In this new weekly update, we're adding a key feature that the game was missing, a way to end the game. That may sound insignificant, but we thought the game being endless was a great idea at first, letting the players decide the precise moment when they want to stop playing instead of fixing a defined end to each game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/5d3151a7520419e75679329017f5c1541a0b1643.gif[/img]

Seing people play the game has proven us wrong and we decided to give players a main objective : collect first each one of the ten mighty tools currently available, making each game play time around 20 minutes. We hope it will bring a new dynamic into the game and that players will feel more involved.

To go along with it we added a victory panel that we think look pretty neat, it changes according to which color each member of the winning team has picked.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/b0e7ec7c5928ec15b22a89b54c92c2a0b68aa630.gif[/img]

[h2]Team names[/h2]

As Team 1 and Team 2 were pretty boring names, we decided to name each one of our character according to its color and set a team captain, then naming each team after its captain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/8ba9ac89c2b6f12605c34e810deb27c5e3e8bf59.gif[/img]

You'll therefore be able to play as Team Flamingo, or Team Cobalt, or Team Phoenix, or any one of the 25 currently available characters.

notes.content:
[h2]Color System Update[/h2]

When the first demo came out, only 8 colors were available to the players.
It came to our ears that those were not enough so we reworked how coloring works in the game to be able to add more colors easily.

We added 24 colors that work well with our color palette for the players to choose from, we tried adding a bit of everything and we hope you will be able to find one you like.

notes.title: SMYS's Demo has been released!
notes.content:
[h2]The First Demo is OUT[/h2]

[b]You can now try the game for yourself and have a taste of what we are preparing![/b] 

This first demo is pretty barebones with only 1 picking phase and 1 building phase, and while this may not be as content rich as we'd like, we thought it would be best to make sure everything is working fine before moving forward.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/24216f9a936727f3cb5685786786d947e65f427d.png[/img]

Yes, even though we spent countless hours playing the game and fixing stuff, there will be bugs we did not encounter and that we'd appreciate YOUR help for. 

If you find anything suspicious, or run into game breaking bugs, please make use of the included Report Panel. It's located in the settings menu and you can use it to describe what happened before, during, and after the issue so we can investigate properly and hopefuly fix it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/23a7303b98982c6a6e1a0a06cbbc1791db140dda.png[/img]

You can also use it to share with us suggestions about how you'd like to see the game moving forward, what content you would like us to add, anything really.

Next update for the demo is already planned to January 2023 and it will add a new picking phase : Trampolines!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42280611/7eca310b3d302a447a951aaa7ca9866b138389e7.png[/img]

We're also preparing the last graphical rework, which will be what the game will look like at release, more on this later.

If you like the demo please wishlist the game, it really makes a difference.
Let's make this the best we can!
